draft.title: Adaptation and appropriation
card: moves a text into a new form, such as a novel into a film or a play into a graphic novel. The story and characters stay close to the original.
reshapes a text for a new time, place or audience. The writer keeps some of the original but changes the setting, voice or focus.

Because an appropriation changes the context, it can change what the text means. For example, a story of two feuding families could be set in a modern city school to say something about teenagers today.
Readers who know the original can compare it with the new version and see what was kept and what was changed.
draft.remember: Adaptation changes the form. Appropriation changes the time, place or audience, and so the meaning.

a.q: A publisher turns a well-known novel into a stage play, keeping the same plot and characters. What is this?
opts: An adaptation
An appropriation
A new genre
An allusion
a.why: The text moves into a new form, a play, and the story stays close to the original. That is an adaptation. It is not an appropriation, because the time, place and audience have not been reshaped.
a.clue: What has changed: the form, or the time and place?

b.q: Priya writes a short story that retells an old tale about a lost shepherd. She sets it in a modern Sydney train station, so it speaks to young commuters. What is this?
opts: An appropriation, because it is reshaped for a new time
An adaptation, because it is retold in a short story
An adaptation, because the old tale is kept in a new setting
An appropriation, because it keeps the same form as the tale
b.why: Priya reshapes the tale for a new time, place and audience, and this changes what it can mean. That makes it an appropriation. Retelling in a new setting is tempting to call an adaptation, but an adaptation is defined by a change of form.
b.clue: Look at what Priya changed: the form, or the setting and audience?

b.best: An appropriation, because it is reshaped for a new time

problems.detail: The remember line says appropriation changes the time, place or audience 'and so the meaning', as if the meaning always changes. The card says an appropriation 'can change' what the text means.

The stem does not say what form the 'old tale' was in. If it was an oral folk tale, retelling it as a written short story is arguably a change of form. That makes 'An adaptation, because it is retold in a short story' less clearly wrong. It would help to say the old tale was itself a written story.

check.summary: The answers are sound. The remember line overstates that appropriation always changes the meaning, where the card says 'can'. Question b should say what form the old tale was in, so the form-change distractor is clearly wrong.
